'''Gani Oladimeji Lawal Jr.''' {{Audio|Gani_Oladimeji_Lawal.wav|listen}}(born November 7, 1988) is a Nigerian-American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]].

==High school career==
During his time at [[Norcross High School]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Scoring high on and off the court |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98164440/scoring-high-on-and-off-the-court/ |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=[[The Atlanta Constitution]] |last=Hollis |first=John|date=2 March 2006 |page=J6|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref> Lawal was named to the [[McDonald's All-American Team]], following his senior season, and was Mr. Basketball 2007 in Georgia.<ref>{{cite news |last=Mahone |first=Derrick |title=Couple of champs |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98165332/couple-of-champs/ |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=[[The Atlanta Constitution]] |date=25 March 2007 |page=E1|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref><ref name=ramblinwreck>[http://ramblinwreck.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/lawal_gani00.html Profile] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100316180437/http://ramblinwreck.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/lawal_gani00.html |date=2010-03-16 }} at RamblinWreck.com.</ref>

Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Lawal was listed as the No. 7 power forward and the No. 29 player in the nation in 2007.<ref>[https://rivals.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Gani-Lawal-24449;_ylt=Aue_E2pqsAN1o6JOuBmH5dnXO5B4 Gani Lawal Recruiting Profile]</ref>

==College career==
As a freshman in [[2007–08 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball team|2007–08]], Lawal scored 10 points on 5-of-6 shots, with four rebounds at [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], snapping a streak of six games in single digits.<ref name=ramblinwreck/> He also had a game-high nine rebounds in a 77–64 win over [[Presbyterian Blue Hose men's basketball|Presbyterian]] on January 6, 2008.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20170822135305/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=280060059 Georgia Tech 77, Presbyterian 64 – Recap] Retrieved August 12, 2017.</ref>

As a sophomore in [[2008–09 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball team|2008–09]], Lawal scored a career-best 34 points<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.wtopnews.com/?nid=210&sid=1540255 |title=Georgia Tech beats Vanderbilt 63–51 |access-date=2009-01-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071011120950/http://wtopnews.com/?nid=210 |archive-date=2007-10-11 |url-status=dead }}</ref> in an 85–83 Georgia Tech loss to [[Penn State Nittany Lions basketball|Penn State]], on December 3, 2008.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=283380059 Penn State 85, Georgia Tech 83 – Box score] Retrieved August 12, 2017.</ref> He had a career-high 16 rebounds in a 63–58 win over [[Tennessee State Tigers basketball|Tennessee State]], on December 30, 2008.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20170813104313/http://www.espn.com/ncb/recap?gameId=283650059 Georgia Tech 63, Tennessee St. 58 – Recap] Retrieved August 12, 2017.</ref> He bested that mark by one rebound, when he pulled down 17 in a 70–56 home loss to Duke, on January 14, 2009.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20170822215838/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=290140059 Singler, Henderson stabilize No. 2 Duke against careless Georgia Tech]</ref>

After originally entering the [[NBA draft]] following his sophomore year, Lawal pulled out of the draft on June 14, 2009, to return to Georgia Tech for [[2009–10 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball team|his junior year]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=4257782|title=Lawal opts to return to Yellow Jackets|last=Katz|first=Andy|authorlink=Andy Katz|work=[[ESPN]]|date=June 14, 2009|access-date=August 12, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Hummer |first=Steve |title=Season on his shoulders |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98164724/season-on-his-shoulders/ |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=[[The Atlanta Constitution]] |date=31 January 2010 |pages=C1, C8|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref> As a junior, Lawal led the team in field-goal percentage and blocked shots.<ref name=scouthoops>[http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=8&c=1&nid=1406628 Gani Lawal Profile] at scout.com.</ref>

==Professional career==
Lawal was drafted by the [[Phoenix Suns]] with the 46th overall pick in the [[2010 NBA draft]]. On August 1, 2010, he signed a three-year deal with the Suns.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://archive.azcentral.com/sports/suns/articles/2010/08/01/20100801phoenix-suns-sign-gani-lawal.html|last=Coro|first=Paul|title=Phoenix Suns sign Gani Lawal to three-year deal|work=[[The Arizona Republic]]|date=August 1, 2010|access-date=August 12, 2017}}</ref> On November 16, 2010, he was assigned to the [[Iowa Energy]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/iowa/lawal_101116.html|title=Phoenix Suns Assign Gani Lawal To Iowa]</ref> He was recalled by the Suns on December 19 and made his NBA debut on December 31, recording one foul in two minutes of action against the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/l/lawalga01/gamelog/2011/ Gani Lawal 2010-11 Game Log]</ref> His season was later ended on January 6 after he suffered a torn ACL.

During the [[2011 NBA lockout]], Lawal played for [[Zastal Zielona Góra]] of the [[Polish Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.azcentral.com/sports/suns/articles/2011/09/07/20110907phoenix-suns-gani-lawal-poland.html|title=Phoenix Suns' Gani Lawal signs with Polish club|last=Coro|first=Paul|work=The Arizona Republic|date=September 8, 2011|access-date=August 12, 2017}}</ref> After the lockout ended, he returned to the United States. However, he was waived by the Phoenix on December 9, 2011,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://archive.azcentral.com/sports/suns/articles/2011/12/09/20111209phoenix-suns-vince-carter-gani-lawal.html|title=Phoenix Suns waive Vince Carter, Gani Lawal|last=Coro|first=Paul|work=The Arizona Republic|date=December 9, 2011|access-date=August 12, 2017}}</ref> and three days later, signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. He was waived by the Spurs on December 22 prior to the start of the regular season.

On December 27, 2011, Lawal signed with the [[Xinjiang Flying Tigers]] to replace the outgoing [[Kenyon Martin]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.niubball.com/2011/12/kenyon-martin-leaves-xinjiang-to-be-replaced-with-gani-lawal/|title=Kenyon Martin leaves Xinjiang, to be replaced with Gani Lawal|last=Pastuszek|first=Jon|date=December 27, 2011|access-date=August 12, 2017}}</ref> He appeared in 17 games for Xinjiang before being released by the club prior to the start of the [[2012 CBA Playoffs]]. He subsequently returned to Zastal, but lasted just three games. In April 2012, he signed with the [[LNB Pro A|French League]] club [[Chorale Roanne]] for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/91382/chorale-roanne-tabs-gani-lawal.html|title=Chorale Roanne tabs Gani Lawal|last=Carchia|first=E.|work=Sportando.com|date=April 15, 2012|access-date=August 12, 2017}}</ref>

In August 2012, Lawal joined the [[Lega Basket Serie A|Italian League]] team [[Virtus Roma]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/94640/virtus-roma-officially-lands-gani-lawal.html|title=Virtus Roma officially lands Gani Lawal|last=Carchia|first=E.|work=Sportando.com|date=August 19, 2012|access-date=August 12, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Zwerling |first=Jared |title=Agent: Knicks 'interested' in Gani Lawal |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/new-york/knicks/post/_/id/45324 |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=2 June 2013}}</ref> In July 2013, he has a short stint with Chinese [[National Basketball League (China)|NBL]] club Guangzhou Liu Sui.<ref>{{cite web|title=Gani Lawal played two games in NBL with Guangzhou Liu Sui|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/103478/gani-lawal-played-two-games-in-nbl-with-guangzhou-liu-sui.html|work=Sportando.com|date=July 11, 2013|access-date=August 12, 2017}}</ref>

On August 9, 2013, Lawal signed a one-year deal with the [[Latvijas Basketbola līga|Latvian League]] team [[BK VEF Rīga|VEF Rīga]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Gani Lawal officially signs with VEF Riga|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/latvia/104791/gani-lawal-officially-signs-with-vef-riga.html|last=Carchia|first=E.|work=Sportando.com|date=August 9, 2013|access-date=August 12, 2017}}</ref> However, it was reported that he chose not to travel with the team for a Euroleague qualification match on October 1, 2013. The team's coach also said that he was disappointed with Lawal's attitude.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/cups/euroleague/106561/ramunas-butautas-gani-lawal-himself-decided-not-to-travel-with-us.html|title=Ramunas Butautas: 'Gani Lawal himself decided not to travel with us'|last=Carchia|first=E.|work=Sportando.com|date=October 1, 2013|access-date=August 12, 2017}}</ref> Two days later, he parted ways with VEF Rīga before appearing in a game for them.<ref>{{cite web|title=VEF Riga, Gani Lawal officially part ways|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/latvia/106626/vef-riga-gani-lawal-officially-part-ways.html|last=Carchia|first=E.|work=Sportando.com|date=October 3, 2013|access-date=August 12, 2017}}</ref>

On October 5, 2013, Lawal signed with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Pompey|first=Keith |title=Lawal plans to stay |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98165574/lawal-plans-to-stay/ |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |date=8 October 2013 |page=D5|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14435 |title=Sixers sign Gani Lawal, waive Solomon Alabi |access-date=2013-10-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170813060042/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14435 |archive-date=2017-08-13 |url-status=dead }}</ref> However, he was later waived by the 76ers on October 27 after appearing in six preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14669|title=Philadelphia 76ers waive Rodney Williams and Gani Lawal|work=[[Inside Hoops]]|access-date=August 12, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029192039/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14669|archive-date=October 29, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> On November 5, 2013, he signed with the Italian team [[Emporio Armani Milano]] for the rest of the 2013–14 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Olimpia: Gani Lawal is on board|url=https://www.olimpiamilano.com/en/olimpia-gani-lawal-is-on-board/|date=November 5, 2013|work=OlimpiaMilano.com|access-date=August 12, 2017}}</ref>

In August 2014, Lawal signed with [[Trabzonspor B.K.|Trabzonspor]] of the [[Turkish Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Gani Lawal agreed to terms with Trabzonspor|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/130852/gani-lawal-agreed-to-terms-with-trabzonspor.html|access-date=August 12, 2017|work=Sportando.com|date=August 8, 2014}}</ref> On January 31, 2015, he left Trabzonspor and signed with the Greek powerhouse [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Panathinaikos Athens bolsters frontcourt with Lawal|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/5q3nfmo93e3krhqj/panathinaikos-athens-bolsters-frontcourt-with-lawal|access-date=August 12, 2017|work=Euroleague.net|publisher=[[EuroLeague]]|date=January 31, 2015}}</ref> On May 11, 2015, he parted ways with Panathinaikos.<ref>{{cite news|title=Gani Lawal, Panathinaikos part ways|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/greece/160799/gani-lawal-panathinaikos-part-ways.html|access-date=August 12, 2017|work=Sportando.com|date=May 11, 2015}}</ref>

On July 14, 2015, Lawal signed a one-year deal with Emporio Armani Milan, returning to the club for a second stint.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.olimpiamilano.com/en/gani-lawal-is-returning-home/|title=Gani Lawal is returning home|date=July 14, 2015 |website=Olimpiamilano.com|access-date=August 12, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/67ap7da39yvyp6el/milan-adds-rim-protector-lawal-in-the-paint|title=Milan adds rim-protector Lawal in the paint|date=July 14, 2015|website=Euroleague.net|publisher=EuroLeague|access-date=August 12, 2017}}</ref> On November 27, he parted ways with Milano after appearing in three [[2015–16 Lega Basket Serie A|league]] games and five [[2015–16 Euroleague|Euroleague]] games.<ref>{{cite news|title=Lawal leaves EA7 Armani|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/Italy/news/429393/Lawal-leaves-EA7-Armani|access-date=August 12, 2017|website=[[Eurobasket.com]]|date=November 27, 2015}}</ref> On December 1, he was acquired by the [[Delaware 87ers]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Delaware 87ers acquire Gani Lawal|url=http://delaware.gleague.nba.com/news/delaware-87ers-acquire-gani-lawal/|access-date=August 12, 2017|work=NBA.com|publisher=[[National Basketball Association]]|date=December 1, 2015}}</ref> On December 12, he had a season-best game with 10 points and 10 rebounds in a loss to the [[Westchester Knicks]].<ref>{{cite news|title=NBA D-League Stats – 87ers vs Knicks|url=http://stats.nbadleague.com/game/#!/2021500095/|access-date=December 19, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=December 19, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222140026/http://stats.nbadleague.com/game/#!/2021500095/|archive-date=December 22, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> On December 30, he was traded to the Westchester Knicks in exchange for a 2016 second-round pick.<ref>{{cite news|title=Westchester Knicks Acquire Gani Lawal|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=5084392|access-date=August 12, 2017|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=December 30, 2015}}</ref> On January 2, 2016, he made his debut with Westchester in a 106–97 win over Delaware, recording nine points, five rebounds, two steals and one block in 21 minutes.<ref>{{cite news|title=Fredette's Double-Double Leads Knicks Past 87ers|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20160102/DELWES/|access-date=January 2, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=February 27, 2016}}</ref> On February 23, he was traded again, this time to the [[Reno Bighorns]] along with a 2016 fourth-round pick, in exchange for the returning player rights to Ra'shad James and a 2016 sixth-round pick.<ref>{{cite news |date=February 23, 2016 |title=Bighorns Acquire Gani Lawal |work=OurSportsCentral.com |url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/bighorns-acquire-gani-lawal/n-5103928 |access-date=August 12, 2017}}</ref> Three days later, he made his debut for Reno in a 121–115 loss to the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]], recording 11 points and 12 rebounds in 14 minutes.<ref>{{cite news|title=Warriors Take Down Bighorns|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20160226/RNOSCW/|access-date=February 26, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=February 27, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304192139/http://dleague.nba.com/games/20160226/RNOSCW/|archive-date=March 4, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> On April 15, 2016, Lawal signed with UAE basketball club Al-Ahli Dubai.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.asia-basket.com/United-Arab-Emirates/basketball.aspx?NewsID=444306|title=Al Ahli adds Lawal to their roster|work=Asia-Basket.com|date=April 15, 2016|access-date=August 12, 2017}}</ref>

On July 6, 2016, Lawal signed with Italian club [[Pallacanestro Cantù]] for the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=PRIMO COLPO PER LA PALLACANESTRO CANTU' CHE INGAGGIA GANI LAWAL|url=http://www.pallacanestrocantu.com/news.html?id=6001|access-date=August 12, 2017|work=Pallacanestrocantu.com|date=July 6, 2016|language=it}}</ref> On November 29, 2016, he parted ways with Cantù after appearing in nine games.<ref>{{cite web |last=Carchia |first=E. |date=November 29, 2016 |title=Pallacanestro Cantù, Gani Lawal part ways |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/218785/pallacanestro-cantu-gani-lawal-part-ways.html |access-date=August 12, 2017 |work=Sportando.com}}</ref> The next day, he signed with [[Dinamo Sassari]] for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/218873/dinamo-sassari-signs-gani-lawal.html|title=Dinamo Sassari signs Gani Lawal|last=Carchia|first=E.|work=Sportando.com|date=November 30, 2016|access-date=August 12, 2017}}</ref>

On July 26, 2017, Lawal signed a one-year deal with Karesi Spor of the [[Turkish Basketball First League]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Cauchi |first=O. |date=July 26, 2017 |title=Gani Lawal inks with KaresiSpor |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/242437/gani-lawal-inks-with-karesispor.html |access-date=August 12, 2017 |work=Sportando.com}}</ref> On January 13, 2018, he moved to [[Petrochimi Bandar Imam BC|Petrochimi Bandar Imam]] of the [[Iranian Basketball Super League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Gani Lawal signs with Petrochimi|url=https://www.sportando.com/en/asia/iran/261002/gani-lawal-signs-with-petrochimi.html|access-date=January 13, 2018|work=Sportando.com|date=January 13, 2018}}</ref>

In May 2019, Lawal signed with the [[Meralco Bolts]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] as their import for the [[2019 PBA Commissioner's Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/gani-lawal-meralco-import-pba-commissioners-cup-a2437-20190503|title=Meralco taps ex-NBA player Gani Lawal as Commissioner's Cup import |last=Leongson |first=Randolph B. |date=May 3, 2019 |publisher=Spin.ph}}</ref>

On July 8, 2020, he has signed with [[Ironi Ramat Gan]] of the [[Liga Artzit (basketball)|Liga Artzit]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/maccabi-ramat-gan-signs-gani-lawal/|title=Maccabi Ramat Gan signs Gani Lawal|date=July 8, 2020|newspaper=Sportando|access-date=July 8, 2020}}</ref> After playing in one preseason game, Lawal parted ways with the team on September 24.<ref>{{cite news |title=Gani Lawal, Maccabi Ramat Gan part ways |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/gani-lawal-maccabi-ramat-gan-part-ways/ |website=Sportando |access-date=September 28, 2020 |date=September 24, 2020}}</ref>

On December 6, 2020, he has signed with [[Al Rayyan Sports Club]] of the [[Qatari Basketball League]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/gani-lawal-signs-with-al-rayyan/|title=Gani Lawal signs with Al Rayyan|date=December 6, 2020|newspaper=Sportando|access-date=December 7, 2020}}</ref>

On February 21, 2021, Lawal signed with [[Champagne Basket|Champagne Châlons-Reims]] in the [[LNB Pro A|Pro A]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Chalons-Reims sign Gani Lawal |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/chalons-reims-sign-gani-lawal/ |website=Sportando |access-date=June 25, 2021 |date=February 21, 2021}}</ref>

On June 16, 2022, he has signed with [[Trotamundos B.B.C.|Trotamundos]] in the [[Venezuelan SuperLiga]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/gani-lawal-signs-in-venezuela/|title=Gani Lawal signs in Venezuela|date=June 16, 2022|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=June 19, 2022|last=Maggi |first=Alessandro }}</ref>

==National team career==
Lawal has been a member of the senior men's [[Nigerian national basketball team]], playing for the team at the [[2013 FIBA Africa Championship]].

==The Basketball Tournament (TBT)==
In the summer of 2017, Lawal competed in [[The Basketball Tournament]] on [[ESPN]] for the number one-seeded FCM Untouchables. Competing for the $2 million grand prize, Lawal averaged 6.7 points, 6.7 rebounds and 1.3 steals per game while shooting 62% from the field. The Untouchables advanced to the Super 16 Round where they were defeated 85–71 by Team FOE, a [[Philadelphia]]-based team coached by [[NBA]] forwards [[Markieff Morris|Markieff]] and [[Marcus Morris (basketball)|Marcus Morris]]. Lawal finished the game with 7 points and 7 rebounds in 15 minutes.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.thetournament.com/bracket/game-51 |title=Game 51 | the Basketball Tournament |access-date=2018-02-07 |archive-date=2018-02-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180207005234/https://www.thetournament.com/bracket/game-51 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Lawal is the son of American Michelle, and Nigerian Gani Sr. He has two sisters, Khalilah and Chasitie, and one brother, Khalil.<ref name=scouthoops/>
